subject: sociology
title: Functionalism in Education: Critiques & Evaluation
welcome_lead: Bowles, Bourdieu and Willis ask: whose meritocracy?
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology functionalism education critiques Marxism Bourdieu Willis.
final_note: Functionalism describes the school's claim; critics test the claim.

concepts.def: Bowles & Gintis — meritocracy is ideology, not reality.
Unspoken lessons of obedience, punctuality, hierarchy.
Functionalism assumes consensus that may not exist.

walkthroughs.body_html: Bowles & Gintis (1976): meritocracy is a myth. Achievement depends on family background, not ability — IQ matters less than parental income. Their correspondence principle shows school's hierarchy, rewards, discipline and timing mirror the workplace, producing obedient workers.

Bourdieu (1977): schools reward cultural capital middle-class kids bring from home. Schools symbolic violence dismisses working-class culture as inferior. Functionalist 'role allocation' is really class reproduction with a meritocratic veneer.

Willis (1977) 'Learning to Labour': 12 'lads' resisted school by mucking about, yet ended in unskilled jobs — partly seeing through the system but reproducing their place. Both Marxist critics deny the consensus that functionalism assumes.

mcqs.q: Bowles & Gintis's term for school mirroring workplace is what?
Bourdieu's term for school's dismissal of working-class culture is what?

free_texts.q: What two-word term names Bowles & Gintis's principle that schools mirror workplaces?
